correctness.rationale: The standard (5,n,2,1) condition is expressed both directly in OR/XOR form and independently as an antichain plus symmetric-difference obstruction. Every one of the 736281 six-subsets and 2629575 seven-subsets of the 31 nonzero length-five vectors is tested by both predicates and they agree everywhere. Exactly 10 six-subsets pass and no seven-subset passes; heredity excludes larger codes. All 10 passing six-subsets are verified to be the K_{2,3} edge families, and all 120 coordinate permutations reproduce one orbit with stabilizer 12. The actual packaged verifier and census were replayed before packaging.

originality.rationale: Published graph-based work covers the constant-weight-two/fan-out-two subproblem, while the inspected general X-code paper explicitly separates that restricted class from unrestricted X-codes and does not give M(5,2,1) or its equality layer. The new statement is the unrestricted rigidity: arbitrary codeword weights do not improve the optimum and every optimum is forced back to K_{2,3}. Targeted published-finding corpus and literature searches found no statement implying the complete ten-code census. Residual risk remains from inaccessible or poorly indexed finite enumerations.
residual_risks: The complete 2003 one-page X-code and fan-out-two proceedings texts were not available in the inspected public copies; an explicit small table there would narrow originality, although the later full-text account characterizes their scope as basic/fan-out-two.
An obscure thesis, industrial note, or unindexed finite computation could contain the same unrestricted five-coordinate census.

value.rationale: This is a natural equality question at the smallest dimension where the same verifier finds strict compaction for the two-error/one-unknown family: dimensions one through four have maxima 1,2,3,4, while dimension five admits six inputs. The result shows that allowing arbitrary fan-out gives no advantage over the minimum-fan-out graph construction exactly at this first nontrivial boundary, and it completely classifies the optimizers. That is a structural finite cutoff rather than an arbitrary slice or a recomputation of a known constant-weight table.
